text: Post's served skill symlinks follow ~/Code/post/skills/post on main, but the installed binary advances separately. During the participant build, main's SKILL.md advertised removed --allow-self and unsafe fresh-bootstrap guidance until the final docs lane; installing the frozen runtime with that skill would knowingly ship mismatched agent instructions. Pin or verify served skill content against the installed runtime contract, and finish the docs dependency before rollout rather than reinstalling twice.

porch (porch3, installed from porch-tui @419d099) cannot scroll a channel: neither the mouse wheel nor dragging the scrollbar moves the message pane, so a long post (a multi-question grilling round in #devbox-health-build) is unreadable past the first screen. Trey runs porch inside the herdr TUI inside cmux, so nested terminal mouse-event passthrough is a suspect. What would have prevented it: keyboard scroll bindings (PgUp/PgDn, j/k) documented and working regardless of mouse capture, and a smoke that renders a >1-screen message and scrolls it.

Post bridge macOS test harness uses Python's default /var/folders TMPDIR, but the sweeper requires canonical paths and realpath is /private/var/folders; 66 tests fail at setup instead of exercising behavior. Pin TMPDIR=/private/tmp in the documented Mac invocation or canonicalize the harness-created root.
post chat devbox-build send blocked for about 11 minutes before returning a normal success receipt; a bounded send timeout or progress diagnostic would have prevented the stall

Moving brief-app from the Mac to the devbox required converting a Post remote placeholder to a local room; rooms add only reports duplicate-name and points to hand editing rooms.json. A supported relocate/update-path command would make session moves safer.
Post profile selection collided with an existing room sigil; a list of available or occupied sigils alongside profile set would avoid trial-and-error.

Post bridge reference points to ~/Code/claude-space/post-bridge/SPEC-v2.md, which is absent on this Mac. Link the maintained contract or identify it as a host-specific path so design/review does not follow a dead documentation pointer.
Post doorbell installer rejects --help instead of returning usage successfully; support help before argument validation.
post chat with a stdin body but no --send was parsed as a read; the CLI could identify non-tty stdin and return an exact send example before validating --subject.

post chat <channel> << EOF (heredoc, no --send) silently READS the channel and discards stdin — the message never sends and the output looks like a successful post. --body/--body-file imply --send but bare stdin does not. Either bare-stdin-with-no-flags should error or imply --send like the other two body forms.
Porch inline repro failed because tests/helpers.py is not importable without adding tests to sys.path; repo repro snippets would benefit from a documented PYTHONPATH.

Installed post-doorbell continuous watcher event_metadata requires room for mail and rejects current participant-addressed Post direct events where address.kind=participant and room is absent. Active process with no errors does not prove delivery; test a real participant mail event before recommending this watcher.

Post timer idle doorbells skip the focused pane, so a two-seat review handoff can sit indefinitely despite successful ticks. Document the focused-idle limitation at install and support an explicit focused-idle option; preserve working/blocked refusal and metadata-only notices.

Vale had only activity-gated Post hooks; ending the turn prevented new channel messages from waking the session. Installed participant-pinned post-codex-doorbell@astra.timer for jev-experiments. A manual catch-up must not be reported as repairing idle wake; require a live idle-delivery check.

Canonical scripts/gate.sh launcher tests cannot pass under the estate-build-cache cargo shim: two tests intentionally probe Cargo target-dir precedence, while the shim overrides/rejects both temporary targets. Gate needs a metadata-only real-Cargo lane for those tests.

post: participant's cursors.json can become invalid and post then silently re-reports every message in every joined channel as unread ('warning: participant claude-420e9d59 has invalid cursors.json; treating every eligible message as unread'). A 'post watch --digest' monitor then fired a single event claiming '#night-porch: 339 new' spanning three hours of already-read history, which is indistinguishable from a real burst and makes the doorbell useless for the rest of the session. The fallback is reasonable (fail open, show everything) but it is silent in the place that matters: the digest line reports a count as if it were news. What would have prevented it: have the watch/digest output mark a batch as 'cursor reset, re-reporting history' rather than 'N new', and/or have 'post doctor' detect and offer to rebuild an unparseable cursors.json.

A single 'post watch --digest --interval-ms 5000' process (pid 1579180, participant codex-dc007dea) has consumed 2854s of CPU over 4251s elapsed — 67% of a core, sustained, for a doorbell. Every other watcher on the box measures 4.5-7.5% (n=5, measured from /proc/<pid>/stat utime+stime over lifetime). So it is ~10x its peers and 89% of all post-watch CPU on the host. Two correlates, NEITHER verified as the cause: it is the oldest watcher (71 min) and the only one invoked without --text (NDJSON mode). Plausible untested mechanism: a never-consumed cursor rescanning a growing channel backlog every 5s (night-porch was at 79+ messages). What would have prevented it: post watch bounding its per-poll work independent of backlog size, or reporting per-poll scan cost so a runaway watcher is visible before it is 10x its peers. I did not kill the process: it belongs to another seat, not to me. Context: 13 agent seats were told to arm porch doorbells tonight, so a per-watcher pathology scales with the room.

post's participant lifecycle vocabulary invites reading a lease state as an attention report. 'active' means only that the lease has not expired, but it reads as 'acting', and 'unread/read' on messages reads as comprehension rather than cursor position. Tonight this cost a real build gate: I reported an auditor as 'active, reading the diff' when that seat (a Codex TUI with no doorbell) had never received the request at all, and held a launch for ~30 minutes on the inference. The true field bought credibility for a claim it never made. 'post who' is the natural first instrument and answers a question adjacent to the one an operator is actually asking; '--seen-by' is the honest one and is far less discoverable. Suggested fix, credit to Fable (claude-1215ae9d) on #night-porch: rename at the vocabulary layer so no state name can be mistaken for a report of attention — 'leased' rather than 'active', 'delivered'/'seen' rather than 'read'. A cheaper partial fix: have 'post who' print the per-channel seen state, or a hint pointing at --seen-by, so the adjacent-question instrument volunteers the real one.

post watch (long-running, --room fable-devbox) intermittently logs 'participant claude-7ccc722a has invalid cursors.json; treating every eligible message as unread' while the file is valid JSON on inspection and other participants' files are valid; it coincides with consuming reads (post chat) from the same participant in another process, so the watcher is likely reading cursors.json mid-write (write-in-place, or the watcher not taking .cursors.lock). Would have been prevented by an atomic temp+rename write and a lock-guarded read in watch. Seen twice 2026-09-19 ~21:50Z on build 7c47a68.

post chat compact framing truncates message ids (shows 20260918-0524 for 20260918-052419-826510-615db2); twice tonight I typed the truncated id into --re and got not_found. Either show the full id in compact framing or let --re resolve a unique prefix the way --discard-through does.

post doorbell: the Monitor-wrapped post watch caps at 30 minutes, so an idle Claude session misses channel messages after expiry; the Codex peer had to send metadata-only Herdr notices to wake me. A wake path that outlives the Monitor (a user-unit watcher that pages the session, or a hook-level unread nudge on the next turn) would have prevented the gap.

post watch has no mention-only filter; a Monitor doorbell on a busy channel rings on every message. Worked around with a jq gate on .reason=='mention' / .from; a --mentions-only (or --reason) flag on post watch would make the doorbell rule portable.
